title: India Summoned the American Envoy. The US Just Struck a Ship With 24 Indians on Board.
excerpt: New Delhi handed Washington a formal protest after a US aircraft fired on the tanker Settebello off Oman, leaving three Indian seafarers missing. The diplomatic fallout comes days before Modi and Trump are expected to meet at the G7.
body:
India took the rare step of summoning a senior American diplomat on Wednesday after a US military aircraft fired on a commercial tanker carrying 24 Indian crew members off the coast of Oman, leaving three seafarers missing and plunging an already strained relationship into its most uncomfortable moment in months.

Nagaraj Naidu, Additional Secretary for the Americas in India's Ministry of External Affairs, called in Jason Meeks, the US Chargé d'Affaires in New Delhi, and handed him a formal diplomatic protest — known as a démarche — over the strike on the Palau-flagged tanker Settebello.

"We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel Settebello off the coast of Oman," the foreign ministry said in a statement. "The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end."

## What Happened

US Central Command said the Settebello was transiting the Gulf of Oman when an American aircraft "fired precision munitions into the ship's engine room" after the crew "repeatedly failed to comply with directions from American forces." The military said the vessel had violated the US blockade of Iranian ports by attempting to transport oil from Iran.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported the tanker suffered an engine room fire roughly 20 nautical miles northeast of Oman's port of Sohar. Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 were rescued. Three remain missing.

This was not an isolated incident. US Central Command has now disabled eight vessels during its blockade of Iran-related shipping, which began on 13 April after Iran severely curtailed traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway carried roughly a fifth of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas before the war.

## The Diplomatic Calculus

The timing makes this particularly fraught. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump are widely expected to hold bilateral talks on the sidelines of the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France, beginning 15 June. Trade, visas, energy cooperation, and H-1B visa policy are all on the agenda.

India has tried to walk a careful line throughout the Iran conflict. As the world's third-largest oil importer, it depends heavily on Gulf energy supplies. It has 8 million citizens working across the Gulf states. And it has been quietly negotiating with both Washington and Tehran to keep supply chains open.

But the Settebello strike made neutrality harder. India's foreign ministry did not blame the US by name in its public statement, but the summoning of the Chargé d'Affaires — the most senior American diplomat in New Delhi at present — was an unmistakable signal.

The démarche was the second direct diplomatic confrontation between the two countries over the Iran war. India had earlier raised concerns about the safety of Indian nationals on commercial vessels in the region.

## Eight Million Reasons to Worry

The immediate concern is human. India has one of the world's largest merchant marine workforces, with hundreds of thousands of seafarers employed on international vessels. The Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz remain among the most heavily trafficked maritime corridors on earth — and among the most dangerous since the Iran war began in late February.

Beyond the seafarers, approximately 8 million Indian citizens live and work in Gulf Cooperation Council countries. Many are employed in construction, retail, and services in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman. Escalation in the region directly threatens their safety and livelihoods.

The broader economic stakes are equally stark. India imports roughly 90 per cent of its crude oil. The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has already pushed Brent crude above $95 per barrel, driven the rupee to record lows near 97 per dollar, and forced the Reserve Bank of India into a series of emergency measures to defend the currency.

## What Comes Next

The G7 bilateral between Modi and Trump will now carry additional weight. India's trade minister, Piyush Goyal, said last week that the two countries are moving toward the first tranche of a bilateral trade agreement, potentially by mid-July. India is also pushing for preferential tariff treatment and wants the H-1B visa issue on the table.

But the Settebello strike has introduced a new variable. New Delhi's willingness to publicly protest an American military action — even one directed at a vessel allegedly violating the Iran blockade — signals that the safety of Indian nationals is a red line it will not quietly accept being crossed.

Search and rescue operations for the three missing Indian seafarers are continuing. The Indian embassy in Oman is coordinating with local authorities.

"Free and unimpeded navigation through international waterways should be restored at the earliest," the foreign ministry said. The statement was addressed to Washington. But it could just as easily have been addressed to Tehran.

nri_angle: India's 8 million citizens in Gulf states face growing risks from the Iran-US conflict. The diplomatic standoff over civilian shipping adds a new layer of tension to the India-US relationship that directly affects diaspora safety and the upcoming Modi-Trump G7 bilateral.
